newsitem.title: UK: UK preliminary Q2 GDP rises 0.9 pct vs Q1.
newsitem.headline: UK preliminary Q2 GDP rises 0.9 pct vs Q1.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics released the following preliminary UK gross domestic product data for the second quarter of 1997. Data as last reported in brackets -
Index (base 1990,
Pct change on qtr 0.9 0.9 (0.9) 0.6
Pct change yr/yr 3.4 3.1 (3.1) 2.5
NOTE - Q2 GDP forecast up 0.9 quarter on quarter and up 3.4 percent year on year.
GDP EXCLUDING OIL AND GAS EXTRACTION.
Pct change on qtr 1.0 1.0 (1.0) 0.5
Pct change yr/yr 3.6 3.1 (3.1) 2.3
OVERALL GDP BREAKDOWN -
INDEX Q2/Q197 Q297/Q296
Distribution,hotels,catering 112.7 1.3 3.0
Total service industries 117.3 1.3 4.5
The ONS said it was estimated that the output of the manufacturing industries was broadly flat in Q2.
Total output of the production industries posted small overall growth in the second quarter as some energy supply growth compensated for a slowdown in the output of the extraction industries.

It said service sector output grew at the same rate as the previous quarter. Services growth was widespread. Business services continue to show the highest growth and the transport and communication, and distribution, hotels and catering industries also grew strongly.
All components in services, including the motor trades, contributed to growth.
The next estimate of Q2 GDP will be published on August 21, when hard data are available for income and expenditure.
A full set of national accounts will be issued on September 23 while preliminary third quarter GDP will be released on October 24, the ONS said.
British gross domestic product has now chalked up 21 successive quarters of growth, since the economy troughed in the second quarter of 1992.
There is little estimated change in the output of agriculture, forestry and fishing output in the second quarter.
The ONS saw a temporary moderation in the construction industry in the second quarter.
There is an estimated decline in the output of the extraction industries, partly because mild weather cut demand for fuel.

Other services grew at a similar rate as in the first quarter but there was a small decline in the growth rate of public administration and defence. Recreation, sport and culture showed strong growth, the ONS said.
